newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Suharto's daughter seeks political support.
newsitem.headline: Suharto's daughter seeks political support.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto's eldest daughter acknowledged on Tuesday a link with the head of the country's largest Moslem organisation, underscoring her powerful role in the ruling Golkar party.

Siti Hardianti Rukmana, a prominent businesswoman, was quoted as saying by the official Antara news agency there was nothing wrong in gaining support ahead of the country's May 29 parliamentary elections.
Rukmana is the only one of Suharto's six children deeply involved in politics and she usually eschews public comment on her role.
But she has become the focus of much attention since she appeared in public last week with Abdurrahman Wahid, head of the 34-million strong Nahadlatul Ulama (NU) Moslem organisation.
While it is a non-political group, NU wields much influence in this Moslem majority nation, and many of its members are close to the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP).

Wahid's support would be a feather in Rukmana's cap since he has often criticised the government and is known to be close to Megawati Sukarnoputri, popular daughter of late founding president Sukarno and Indonesia's best-known opposition figure.
Wahid took Rukmana, popularly known as Tutut, to an informal meeting last Wednesday in the East Java town of Sidoarjo, where both of them appeared before some 10,000 NU members.
They plan two similar joint public appearances within the next two weeks.

"It's logical that contestants are trying to collect as many votes as possible. But this effort should be done in line with existing rules and in the frame of national unity," Rukmana was quoted as saying by Antara.

"It is not aimed at other parties," she said, referring to newspaper comments that the alliance was aimed at undercutting PPP votes. The PPP, the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) and Golkar are the only groups permitted to contest elections.

PPP chairman Ismail Hasan Metareum has been quoted by Antara and newspapers as saying Wahid's moves were aimed at affecting his party's performance in the elections and would help Golkar penetrate the Moslem-based party's strongholds.
But Wahid denied the allegations. He was quoted as saying this week that the PPP should instead imitate Golkar to win the hearts of the members of the NU.
"NU belongs to all three political contestants. No political organisation can claim that NU belongs to them only," Wahid told the Jakarta Post newspaper this week.
Political analyst Mochtar Buchori said that Wahid's public appearances with Rukmana were aimed at a rapprochement with Suharto, whom he has strongly criticised in the past.
"His move aims to create the impression he has no problem with Suharto," Buchori told Reuters.

He also said it was too early to say Wahid had ended his links with Megawati, who was ousted from the leadership of the PDI by a government-backed faction last year. She is not a contestant in the elections.
"It's too early to say that Wahid has left Megawati. In fact they are still good friends," said Buchori who is also a close associate of Megawati.
